subject: Phase 100200 — Additive Harness Workspace Tools
verdict_justification: The phase is broad and largely well-tested: the atomic batch engine, scratchpad, validate, stats, and schema publication all work, and the coverage/size/isolation gates genuinely pass. However two material defects survive: a batch containing two canonical_put operations on the same key commits two simultaneously active revisions (single-slot supersession silently broken), and the shared-bank permission gate is bypassable through the generic/batch tools because it is enforced only on the shared_* wrappers, not on the bank.

issues.title: batch with two canonical_put ops on one key commits two active revisions
issues.why_it_matters: canonical_* promises single-slot semantics: a new put must close the prior revision. Inside `batch`, prior resolution runs at pre-flight before the batch's own creates exist, so the second put cannot see (and therefore cannot close) the first put's row. Both rows land with tx_until NULL.
issues.impact: Two simultaneously active revisions for the same canonical key. canonical_get returns whichever row `ORDER BY tx_from DESC LIMIT 1` happens to win; when both ops share a timestamp (the default `now` is second-precision) the winner is nondeterministic. Downstream code and audit reconstruction see a slot with no well-defined current value.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:138-141 (prior = get_item_by_subject at preflight); crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:179-193 stages only CloseItem{prior}+CreateItem. Reproduction: `printf` two canonical_put ops (key k1, values v1/v2) into `am mcp stdio --db /tmp/adv-can.db` -> batch returns both COMMITTED; follow-up `stats bank=bk` returned {"items_total":2,"items_active":2}. Both staged rows share tx_from "2026-09-19T19:42:41Z".
issues.proposed_fix: Resolve canonical priors at commit time inside the transaction (like triple_add's tx-scoped supersede query), or reject a batch that contains two canonical_put ops for the same (bank,key), or fold same-key puts within a batch so only the last survives.

issues.title: Shared-bank permission gate is bypassable via batch and generic tools
issues.why_it_matters: The phase introduces shared_* wrappers plus a deployment permission flag as the 'strict tenant boundary'. The check lives only in shared_args, so any caller can reach the same bank through `store`, `canonical_put`, `triple_add`, or a `batch` op with bank="shared", and can read it via `stats`/`inspect`. The boundary is enforced by tool name, not by bank.
issues.impact: A deployment that has not enabled the shared surface still accepts writes to and reads from bank `shared`; the documented authorization control does not hold.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:233-255 (gate only in shared_args); crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime.rs:245-259 (resolve_ctx trusts args.bank). Reproduction with default McpOpenOptions (shared_bank_enabled=false): batch store op bank="shared" -> status COMMITTED; `stats bank=shared` -> 1 item; `shared_store` -> code "forbidden".
issues.proposed_fix: Enforce the shared-bank permission at the bank-routing layer (reject bank==SHARED_BANK in resolve_ctx unless enabled), or have batch/preflight reject ops targeting the shared bank when the surface is disabled, rather than gating only the three shared_* entry points.

issues.title: Single-op canonical_put supersession is not atomic
issues.why_it_matters: commit_canonical invalidates the prior row and then inserts the new row as two separate store calls with no surrounding transaction. An error after the invalidate leaves the slot with no active value while the caller's admission telemetry already succeeded.
issues.impact: A transient store failure can silently empty a canonical slot; the new value is lost and the old value is closed. The batch path was deliberately made atomic, which highlights the gap in the single-op path.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/canonical.rs:72-94: store.invalidate_item(...) then store.create_memory_item(...) then record_audit_event(...), all separate calls.
issues.proposed_fix: Route the single-op put through the batch executor (canonical_batch_writes already exists) or wrap the close+create+audit in one store transaction.

issues.title: AC-100200-03 evidence overstates a vacuous scratchpad-isolation test
issues.why_it_matters: The phase file claims the test 'writes a marker to the pad and confirms retrieve returns no scratchpad row'. The test never examines the retrieve response for the marker; its only isolation assertion reads key "zqxj marker", which was never written (the write used key "leak"). The assertion passes for any implementation, including one that leaked.
issues.impact: The negative guarantee (T100200-03 / FR-21) has no effective regression test on the retrieve side. A future change that accidentally persisted scratchpad content would not be caught by this test.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools_tests.rs:154-184; the closing assertion is `s.scratchpad.read("default","bank-a",Some("zqxj marker"),...) .is_err()`. Phase file AC-100200-03 row (roadmap/phase-100200...:435).
issues.proposed_fix: Assert the retrieve hits contain the stored row but none whose id/content came from the pad, or seed the same marker in a durable row and assert exactly one hit; keep the pad write with a real key and assert it is absent from all hits.

issues.title: Phase negative tests for shared category and canonical admission are missing
issues.why_it_matters: The phase's Negative Testing section explicitly requires 'shared_store with invalid semantic category is rejected' and 'canonical_put scoring below admission threshold is rejected'. Neither has a direct test.
issues.impact: Those specific fail-closed paths are unverified; the category path is only exercised indirectly through the generic store tests, and canonical below-threshold is not exercised at all.
issues.evidence: grep over crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools_tests.rs and crates/clio-compliance/src/canonical_tests.rs finds no invalid-category shared test and no below-theta canonical test; only batch store/task/persona/failure/triple rejection is covered (batch_tools_tests.rs:311-355).
issues.proposed_fix: Add one test each: shared_store with category not in the §4.1 whitelist -> rejection; canonical_put under a theta-admit>1 env -> structured rejection with no prior closed.

issues.title: canonical_put always stores snapshot=None, so slots are gist-only
issues.why_it_matters: Canonical slots are meant for exact single values (e.g. primary_database_host), but the MCP handler hardcodes snapshot: None and the schema offers no snapshot parameter. canonical_get therefore returns only the prose gist for a value that is typically an exact identifier.
issues.impact: Tension with FR-5 / PR-4, which say no downstream consumer should be given only the gist when the query concerns a specific value. Callers cannot attach the authoritative snapshot.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:148 (snapshot: None) and 134-156; canonical_get surfaces `value: item.gist` (canonical.rs:153-160).
issues.proposed_fix: Accept an optional snapshot/source_text on canonical_put and pass it through (the store path already supports verified snapshots).

issues.title: validate module doc says notes are masked before storage, but the raw note is persisted
issues.why_it_matters: The header claims 'Non-empty reviewer note (masked before storage)', yet the audit detail stores args.note verbatim; only the returned outcome.note is scrubbed.
issues.impact: A reviewer note containing a secret is written to durable audit telemetry unmasked, contradicting the module's stated contract.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/validate.rs:15-16 vs 147-158, 190-202, 224-235 (raw note in detail) and 245-250 (scrub applied only to outcome).
issues.proposed_fix: Scrub the note once at entry and use the scrubbed value for both the audit detail and the outcome, or correct the header to say masking is output-only.

issues.title: schema_tests.rs contains a garbled duplicated comment from an incomplete edit
issues.why_it_matters: A half-edited comment line repeats a phrase ('...the additive every bound tool: the Core catalog plus the additive') and the test replaced an exact set-equality assertion with a presence loop.
issues.impact: Cosmetic, but it signals the test was mechanically weakened when additive tools inflated the catalog; the pack is now only presence-checked, not completeness-checked.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/schema_tests.rs:18-33 (the comment and the removed `assert_eq!(tools.len(), catalog.len())`).
issues.proposed_fix: Fix the comment and assert catalog_defs() names == bound tools (or the expected core+additive set) rather than mere containment.

findings.title: batch with two canonical_put ops on one key commits two active revisions
findings.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/batch_preflight.rs:138-141 and 179-193; reproduced via `am mcp stdio` (two canonical_put key k1 -> both COMMITTED; stats items_active=2, both tx_until NULL, identical tx_from).
findings.recommendation: Resolve canonical priors at commit time in-transaction, or reject/fold duplicate-key canonical ops within a batch; add a one-active-revision regression test.
findings.resolution: Added `BatchWrite::CanonicalPut` (clio-store/src/batch_model.rs). The batch executor now resolves the active slot row for the item's subject INSIDE the transaction (`active_item_id_by_subject_tx` in sqlite_memory.rs/postgres_memory.rs) and stages close+create+audit in the same tx (batch_sqlite.rs / batch_postgres.rs). `batch_preflight::canonical_preflight` no longer resolves priors at pre-flight. Regression tests: `clio-mcp batch_tools_canonical_tests::two_canonical_puts_one_key_in_one_batch_leave_one_active_revision`, `clio-compliance canonical_tests::two_puts_one_key_in_one_batch_leave_one_active_revision`, `clio-store batch_tests::sqlite_canonical_put_effect_supersedes_in_transaction`, and PG coverage in `batch_pg_tests::postgres_batch_parity`. Tests assert exactly one active revision plus one closed (tx_until set) revision.

findings.title: Shared-bank permission gate is bypassable via batch and generic tools
findings.evidence: crates/clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs:233-255 (gate only on shared_*); crates/clio-mcp/src/runtime.rs:245-259; reproduced: batch store bank=shared COMMITTED while shared disabled and shared_store returned forbidden.
findings.requirement_ref: roadmap/phase-100200 Task 4 + Security Constraints; requirement.md FR-22 / §4.9.5.A
findings.recommendation: Enforce shared-bank authorization at the bank-routing layer (resolve_ctx or preflight), not only in shared_args.
findings.resolution: Enforced the shared-bank permission at the bank-routing layer: `McpState::resolve_ctx` (clio-mcp/src/runtime.rs) now rejects `bank="shared"` with `forbidden` unless `shared_enabled` is true, so batch/store/canonical_put/triple_add/stats/retrieve cannot bypass it. `shared_args` still forces the bank and requires `actor`. Negative tests: `additive_tools_shared_tests::shared_bank_is_unreachable_through_generic_tools_when_disabled` (stats + generic store denied, 0 rows) and `batch_tools_canonical_tests::batch_cannot_reach_shared_bank_when_surface_disabled` (batch op denied, `shared_*` wrapper still forbidden).

findings.title: Single-op canonical_put supersession is not atomic
findings.evidence: crates/clio-compliance/src/canonical.rs:72-94: invalidate_item then create_memory_item then record_audit_event as separate calls.
findings.recommendation: Run the close+create+audit in one transaction (reuse canonical_batch_writes / BatchStore).
findings.resolution: Single-op `canonical_put` now routes through `state.batch.apply_batch(&[BatchWrite::CanonicalPut{..}])` (clio-mcp/src/additive_tools.rs), so close+create+audit commit in one transaction. The non-transactional `commit_canonical`/`canonical_batch_writes` helpers were removed from clio-compliance/src/canonical.rs (it now owns key naming + reads only). Failure-injection test `canonical_tests::canonical_put_failure_after_close_rolls_back_the_slot` proves a create failure after the staged close rolls the whole slot back (prior stays active).
